title: brain: theOS's memory, one folder, one schema, one door
note: brain is theOS's memory and its single source of truth: one JSON doc per thing, kept in one folder, theOS/brain/, with a schema per type, the reflection (what a new doc supersedes) and the trace (which AIP and author wrote it). Every read and write goes through one door, the brain command and its skill (d-5bce, d-87d6), over plain functions aip-a195 also serves by MCP (d-432d). Learned from rs-a3fa.

questions.q: Is brain's direction right: a JSON doc per thing, JSON Lines for whatever only grows, a JSON Schema per type, binaries named by content hash, and every internal reference pinned as path@full commit SHA?
options: Yes, take it into aip-836d's Understand
Change it: tell me what

questions.q: brain, two simplifications the review proposes against your direction (d-0e44, d-1fee): keep each list that only grows as a JSON array with a prefix check instead of JSON Lines, and compute a link's version from git (the commit that added the citing line) instead of storing path@SHA?
options: Both (recommended: no history was rewritten yet, and the static apps cannot read git objects)
Keep JSON Lines and stored pins, as decided
Only the arrays
Only the computed version

questions.q: aip-836d's link versions (c5): defer them until a correction is traced to a link whose target moved? Most links point at docs that never change or change all the time, so the flag would carry little signal, and showing it needs a publish step no AIP builds yet.
options: Defer c5 until such a correction (recommended)
Keep c5 in checkpoint 4
questions.answer: Don't defer (Samuel, 10:47): c5 is in checkpoint 3.

questions.q: Decision ids: with many threads at once, keep D-n numbers, or switch to hash ids with D-n as a label?

Hash ids, D-n as a label

questions.q: Should brain's command be the only door from the start (the check fails any commit that changed a doc without it), or advisory for one checkpoint first?

Advisory for one checkpoint first

questions.q: Should brain's verbs also be served over MCP, so aip-a195's mod, the apps and other sessions use the same door, or stay a command and a skill for now?
options: A command and a skill now; MCP with aip-a195 (recommended)
MCP from the start

questions.q: Is withdraw (a doc stops holding with no successor, with its reason kept) a verb you want, or must every doc that stops holding be superseded by a newer one?
options: Withdraw, with its reason, only from an AIP's event (recommended)
Only supersede

questions.q: Hash ids (d-ac7d): do d-1b6c to d-072e, aip-31df to aip-f4e2 and the other numbered docs keep their names as labels, or are they renamed?
options: Renamed once, every link rewritten in the same commit (recommended: one name per doc, nothing to keep in step)
Kept as labels beside the hash id

questions.q: How strict is brain add about the reflection: refuse a doc whose author skipped a candidate brain reflect listed, or let the reviewer judge?
options: The reviewer judges; brain refuses only a supersede of a doc that did not hold (recommended: whether a doc replaces another needs judgement)
brain add refuses
questions.answer: The reviewer judges: "reviewer to judge" (Samuel, in the aip-836d thread, 2026-11-01)

questions.q: Hash ids for the docs that exist now: you said "you can rename them" (d-3a9c). A review points out a third way: old docs keep their D-n and AIP-n ids, and only new docs get hash ids. Old ids were made one at a time and never collide, so this needs no migration, no exception to history only growing, and no rename map, and prose like "(d-5bce)" keeps working. Which?
options: Keep the old ids; only new docs get hash ids (recommended)
Rename every doc once (d-3a9c as written)

questions.q: Where do theOS sessions start? The brain prime hook and theOS/CLAUDE.md load only if a session's working folder is theOS/ (the repository root's .claude is legacy and not changed).
options: theOS threads start in theOS/ (recommended)
At the repository root, with the hook added to the root .claude by an exception

who: Samuel Andert, who must trust that the agents follow what he decided, as it stands now.
avenMAIA and its agents, which read brain before they act and write to it as they work.
Anyone who later asks why something is the way it is.
problem.experience: Decisions, words and history were kept in chat and in files edited in place: a newer decision did not say what it replaced, outdated words came back, and nobody could tell which step wrote what.

items.text: Decisions were listed oldest first, and a newer one did not say which older one it replaced (the dated decision docs, before d-cbd4).
avenCEO had to be renamed by hand across 13 types, 25 terms and three apps, twice (d-e2d9, d-81c7).
A read flag on 58 sources claimed a global truth that was per intent (d-418a).
A link is a bare path, and the file behind it changes (d-0e44).

problem.baseline: Now: one JSON doc per thing in theOS/ (the counts are read off when Gate A is asked); the reflection and the trace computed by the apps; no schema, no check that history only grows, links by bare path.
whys: You can't be sure the agents follow what holds now. Why? Old and new decisions sat side by side, edited in place, without saying which replaces which.
Why? Memory had no rules: no schema per type, no history that only grows, no reflection, links that move.
Root cause: brain has no schema, and nothing enforces the reflection, the trace or the growth of history.
truths: Git keeps every version of every file; a commit SHA names exactly one.
What is computed from a log that only grows cannot drift from it.
A JSON Schema is checked by a program, without judgement.
Whether a new decision replaces an old one needs judgement: an agent proposes it, the decision records it.
A program that is the only way to write can refuse a bad write before it lands; a check after the fact can only fail the commit.
assumptions: One JSON doc per thing stays fast enough for the apps and the command at a few hundred docs.
An event can be typed by hand, so the check proves an event exists, not that the command wrote it; the door is kept by the check, not by force.

Until aip-6fb1's pipeline runs checks on the server, the check runs from a git pre-push hook that brain prime installs, and avenMAIA runs brain check on every merged tree; a thread that removes the hook is caught there.
problem.risk: Can be undone: every change is files in git.

reuse.what: theOS/ui/wiki.js: the crawl, the backlinks, W.trace and W.stepAt
reuse.use: Used: links, backlinks, the trace and the step (the functions trace and stepAt) are computed there already; brain loads the same file.
Moved into the one holds() that brain and the apps load.
Learned from: a frozen verb protocol with a conformance test; one CLI as the only door and hash ids; edits that quote the version read; supersede, never delete.
Learned from, not touched: a log that only grows is checked by comparing it with its earlier version.

options.name: One door over the JSON docs in git: a command with fixed verbs and its skill, MCP for aip-a195; the check behind it
options.note: The direction you approved (d-1fee, d-260c, d-0020) with the door (d-5bce, d-87d6, d-d9fd). The verbs come from gbrain's frozen protocol, Beads' only-door CLI, Basic Memory's guarded edits and Graphiti's never-delete supersession (rs-a3fa).

options.name: Free writes to files, with only the check after
options.note: Rejected (d-5bce, d-87d6): an agent learns of a bad write only when the commit fails, and nothing teaches it the verbs.

options.name: A memory library: a model extracts facts, vector or graph search finds them (mem0, Zep, Cognee)
options.note: Rejected: brain records decisions explicitly; a model inside the door makes it non-deterministic. mem0 itself moved from model-chosen updates and deletes to add-only (src-3dd8).

options.name: A database
options.note: Rejected: git already versions, diffs and reviews files; a database would need its own history and review.

claims.promise: Every JSON doc in theOS (in brain/, aip/ and avenCEO/) has a type with a type doc, and matches the JSON Schema inside it. by is always an author doc; every type a newer doc can supersede has about (topic words); a correction event names its cause (outdated-decision, outdated-word, missed-supersede or other), set from Samuel's words or, at Learn, by a fresh checker, never by the agent whose work was corrected.
claims.fails: A misspelt field, a missing or misspelt type, or a free-text author passes unseen.
claims.check: Validated with ajv; each schema rejects a planted bad doc of its type; every current doc passes.

claims.promise: brain protocol v1 is the one door for reads: every verb is a plain function brain.mjs exports; the command gives every verb's documented answer and error codes; the skill teaches them; brain prime runs at session start from theOS/.claude/settings.json and theOS/CLAUDE.md names it first (d-6b87).
claims.fails: brain prime shows a superseded doc as holding, or misses something that waits for Samuel; or a verb answers differently than v1 says.
claims.check: A test calls every exported verb on the fixed docs in theOS/brain/test/ (with superseded docs, docs superseded in part and open questions planted) and through the command line, and compares both with the expected answers; the hook, CLAUDE.md's first line and the skill file name brain prime. Agents reading raw files instead is the outcome's to measure.

claims.promise: One migration commit opens checkpoint 2, written by brain as one event of aip-836d at Build (d-3a9c, d-f83e): every doc gets a flat hash id, intents and avenCEO's docs included; the docs brain keeps move into brain/ (the Sources app becomes brain's app); every supersedes entry takes the form {doc, part, what}; every reference, paths and old names in text alike (d-0e44, aip-836d; quotes included; OLD-AIP-n is legacy and kept), is rewritten as an id, events included; review docs' prompts stay verbatim. theOS/brain/renames.json keeps each old name and path with its new id, and the commit's SHA: the one exception c2 accepts. Legacy files outside theOS/ are not changed; their old paths are looked up in renames.json.
claims.fails: A doc, an app or a text inside theOS/ still uses an old name or path, an old name can no longer be looked up, or another commit claims the exception.
claims.check: After the migration brain check finds no old name and no path used as a link anywhere in theOS/ (renames.json and review prompts excepted); brain get resolves every old name; c2 accepts history rewritten only in the commit renames.json names.

claims.promise: Every doc changed in a commit is covered by an event added in that commit, by an author doc (an intent's own doc by its new events); metrics and lessons only at Learn (d-f960, d-87d6).
claims.fails: A doc changes that no AIP step wrote.
claims.check: brain check fails a planted edit with no event, an event by a free string, and a measurement written outside Learn; a planted normal merge of a branch with new docs passes.

claims.promise: Every new doc gets a random hash id minted by brain add (d-ac7d), so parallel threads almost never pick the same one; when two do, the merge fails, and one is minted again.
claims.fails: Two threads create the same id and one silently overwrites the other.
claims.check: A test makes two branches add a decision each to the same intent and merges them: no clash, the index written again, both events kept by the merge driver. A test with two branches adding the same id expects the merge to fail.

claims.promise: No list is kept twice: session.decisions, session.intents and the definition's copied lists are deleted and computed by the apps from links; the index docs and ids.json equal their folders because only brain index writes them.
claims.fails: A copy drifts, as session.intents did.
claims.check: brain check fails an index doc that differs from its folder, and a planted copied list in a session or the definition.

claims.promise: One reflection for every type: a new doc's supersedes entries ({doc, part, what}) each point at a doc that held at the parent commit; what holds is computed, never stored. The candidates the doc leaves unsuperseded are recorded in its event by brain add, and the reviewer judges them (d-0a3f).
claims.fails: A doc supersedes something that no longer held, or points at nothing.
claims.check: brain add and brain check refuse a planted supersede of a doc already superseded at the parent, and one of a missing doc; a planted add records its left candidates in the event.

claims.promise: Links are brain's graph: a link is an id, never a path; every id inside a doc resolves to a doc, and each link's type is the field it sits in; brain get returns links and backlinks by type. brain check warns, without failing, when a doc that holds cites one that was superseded (d-072e).
claims.fails: A link points at nothing, or a holding doc quietly rests on a superseded one.
claims.check: brain check fails a planted id that resolves to nothing and a planted path used as a link, and prints a warning for a planted citation of a superseded doc.

claims.promise: A term that renames a word carries the old word and where the rename applies (a list of folders), and the terms check fails when the old word comes back there, and stays quiet where its other meaning is right. (Ids are renamed by c12's renames.json; c6 is for words.)
claims.fails: A rename sweep misses a place, or a word with two meanings raises a false alarm.
claims.check: A test plants each renamed word once where the rename applies and once where its other meaning is right.

claims.promise: What only grows (an intent's events, a metric's measurements, a session's asks) stays a JSON array that only grows.
claims.fails: History is rewritten and nothing notices.
claims.check: brain check requires the parent's array to be a deep-equal prefix of the new one; a planted edit, deletion or reorder of an old entry fails.

claims.promise: A link's version is computed, never stored: the version cited is the commit that added the citing line (git blame, skipping the migration commit and following moved files); brain get and brain check flag a link whose target changed since, and brain index writes the flags into a file the app reads to show a 'changed since' chip.
claims.fails: A link silently shows content that changed after it was cited.
claims.check: A planted citation made before the migration of a doc changed after it is flagged by brain get, brain check and in the app's file; seeing the chip is part of Gate B's try.

claims.promise: brain's MCP server serves every verb of v1 from the same functions brain.mjs exports, so other sessions and tools use the same door (d-d9fd, d-9271).
claims.fails: A tool reaches brain some other way, or the server answers differently than the command.
claims.check: The verb test of c7 runs once more through the MCP server and requires the same answers and error codes.

outcome.promise: Over the three sessions after checkpoint 3: no correction whose cause is an outdated decision, an outdated word or a missed supersede.
outcome.how: Each correction event names its cause (c1). At Learn the measurement counts them per session from those events; the baseline is the same count over this session's corrections, labelled by a fresh checker at Gate A.

checkpoints.adds: Reads first, needing nothing from aip-31df: holds() moved from avenCEO/app.js into ui/wiki.js (three states: holds, holds in part, superseded); brain prime, holds and get as exported functions and the command; the hook in theOS/.claude/settings.json and the first line of theOS/CLAUDE.md. The skill is written by hand here (brain index writes it from checkpoint 2); links and backlinks are flat until checkpoint 3 groups them by type.

The migration first (c12): brain/, flat hash ids, the supersedes form, ids.json, the Sources app as brain's app. Then, on the final shape and on aip-31df's check command and package.json: schemas in the type docs (written as aip-836d's writes, approved at Gate A); about where a doc can be superseded; brain add, edit, append, index (with the skill) and install; brain check failing a doc changed without an event (d-87d6, the only door from here); copied lists deleted.

The reflection (brain reflect; supersedes checked at the parent; left candidates recorded); the link graph by type and its audit; renamed words and the terms check; lists that only grow; link versions.
brain's MCP server over the same exported functions, needing nothing from another intent (d-9271).

deferred.what: The maintenance pass: a fresh agent turns brain check's warnings and missed supersedes into proposed writes through the same verbs, in an AIP's step
deferred.until: Three sessions without a correction whose cause is a missed supersede, or warnings pile up faster than they are fixed.

deferred.what: brain changes --since <commit>: what changed since a point, for a thread coming back
deferred.until: A thread rereads brain often enough to need it.

deferred.what: A 'valid from' date apart from the commit time
deferred.until: A decision is recorded after it took effect.

deferred.what: brain edit --expect <sha>: refuse an edit of a doc changed since it was read
deferred.until: Two writers share one working tree.

mockup: brain prime at session start: the decisions and terms that hold now, then 'Waits for Samuel' with the open questions and his tasks (the text the hook injects)
brain get on a decision: the doc, 'superseded by' if any, its links and backlinks grouped by type, and 'changed since' beside a link whose target moved

The brain app (today's Sources app, renamed): sources, decisions, sessions, terms, lessons, metrics and authors in one place, each list split into Hold now and Superseded (there today in avenCEO/app.js, kept by the shared holds())
brain has no other new screen; at Gate A these are shown as they are

source.text: Let's settle the schema of our single source of truth for everything we generate in AIPs, learnings and sources: what is a JSON file, what is a list of JSON entries, what is markdown, and what is both. And link every internal git resource by its commit hash, never by a bare file path, because history changes.

protocol.name: brain protocol v1
protocol.what: The one door to brain (d-5bce). One program, theOS/brain/brain.mjs, with these verbs, each a plain function it exports. The command line calls them, and the skill theOS/.claude/skills/brain/SKILL.md, written by brain index from the verb list, teaches them (it loads because theOS threads start in theOS/, d-6b87). An MCP server serves the same functions to other sessions and tools (d-d9fd, d-9271), in aip-836d's last checkpoint. Fields keep their meaning forever; v1 only grows (new verbs, new optional fields). brain writes files; the agent commits them with its other work.

reads.does: Prints the decisions and terms that hold now (id and title) and what waits for Samuel (open questions and his tasks); brain holds <type> gives the rest. A Claude Code hook in theOS/.claude/settings.json runs brain install (from checkpoint 2) and then brain prime at the start of a session and after compaction (when Claude Code shortens a long conversation to fit); theOS/CLAUDE.md names brain prime first.

Lists the docs of a type that hold now, from the one holds() in ui/wiki.js that the apps also use. A doc holds until a newer doc supersedes it (a chain does not bring an old one back); superseded only in part (part is anything but all, whole or left out), it holds in part. The result does not depend on the order branches were merged.

Returns one doc, what supersedes it, and its links and backlinks (a link is any string that is an id), grouped by type from checkpoint 3: the field they sit in, such as supersedes, relates, intents or writes. A link whose target changed since the commit that added it is flagged 'changed since' (c5). An old name (d-0e44, aip-836d) is resolved through theOS/brain/renames.json.
Lists the docs of the same type that hold (wholly or in part) and share a topic word (about) with the draft: the candidates it may supersede. The author judges.

protocol.writes_rule: Every write takes --intent (an AIP) and --by (an author doc). It writes the doc and appends the event to that intent; the agent commits both together, and brain check fails a commit where they are apart. Only metrics and lessons are limited by step: they are written at Learn (d-f960); every other type, corrections included, may be written at any step, Closed too.

writes.does: Mints the doc's id: <prefix>-<hex>, the prefix short for the type and the hex 4 random characters, longer if the id exists on this branch (d-ac7d), and files the doc in its type's folder; decisions are written by avenMAIA, which mints their ids this way. Checks the doc against its type's schema; refuses a supersedes entry ({doc, part, what}: part is all, the default, or part) whose doc does not exist or did not hold, wholly or in part, at the parent commit. Warns about a topic word no other doc uses, showing the closest words in use. Runs brain reflect itself and writes into the event the candidates the doc does not supersede, for the reviewer to judge (d-0a3f). Runs brain index. Answers created or unchanged, and lists what the doc supersedes.
Changes a doc in place for a correction that keeps its meaning (a typo, a title, d-6e78); a change of meaning is a new doc that supersedes it. Answers changed or unchanged.
Adds an entry to the end of a list that only grows (events, measurements, asks). Answers appended.

Writes every index doc from its folder (the static apps cannot list a folder). It runs inside the write that needs it, and the index is listed in that event's writes; it is never edited by hand, so a merge clash in one is resolved by running it again.

Sets up this clone for brain: a git pre-push hook that runs the check when files under theOS/ changed (calling any hook already there), and the merge driver for lists that only grow. Merges of brain's docs happen locally, by avenMAIA; GitHub's merge button ignores merge drivers.

check.does: A module that aip-31df's check command runs on every commit before it is pushed (from the pre-push hook) and that avenMAIA runs on every merged tree. It runs every claim's check below and fails a commit that changed a doc without an event of that commit (d-87d6); an intent's own doc is covered by its new events. A non-merge commit is checked against its parent; a merge commit only for what differs from both parents. Merges resolve with brain index (index docs and ids.json written again) and the merge driver, which keeps both sides' new entries, the first parent's first.

protocol.errors: Every refusal is a fixed code with the fix, for example no_intent (pass --intent <aip id>), schema (field x: expected y), step (a metric is written at Learn; the AIP stands at <step>), not_held (<id> was superseded by <id>).
not: No delete and no withdraw: a doc stops holding only when a newer doc supersedes it through the reflection (d-072e).
No model inside the door: brain never guesses a supersede or a link.
No commits by brain, and no version guard on edit yet: each thread writes its own branch, so clashes show at merge.
protocol.layout: brain/ holds brain's program (brain.mjs, test/), ids.json, renames.json, its app (index.html, app.js: today's Sources app, renamed brain) and every doc brain keeps, in folders by type: brain/sources, brain/decisions, brain/sessions, brain/terms, brain/lessons, brain/metrics, brain/authors. aip/ (the intents) and avenCEO/ (the harness) keep their folders; their docs get ids too. Folders are only where files sit; no link names one.
protocol.ids: Every doc, intents and avenCEO's docs included, is referenced by its id alone, flat, never by a path: a type prefix and random hex (d- and 4 hex characters for a decision, aip- for an intent, src- for a source), unique across theOS. A link is any string that is an id. brain index writes theOS/brain/ids.json, the map from id to file, which brain and the static apps read, so a doc can move between folders without any link changing. Wherever a doc is shown, in the apps, in brain's answers and in text, it reads as its id and its title, "aip-<hex> · brain: theOS's memory" (d-4e7c); no D-n or AIP-n numbers. New decisions and intents get hash ids like every other doc and are ordered by time. ui/wiki.js does the naming (W.name, W.title, W.named), for the apps and for brain.
